findings.summary: A book point is missing from these pages.
findings.evidence: Meaningful exit codes: 0 success, 1 general error, 2 usage error; reserve 64-78 for sysexits.h conventions if you care
findings.fix: Add this point to a page — the fit pass may only add, so it is safe to run.

findings.summary: Every page's blocks are offset by roughly one section from its title, so each page opens with the tail of the previous chapter and closes with the head of the next.
findings.evidence: Page 4 is titled "Quoting, Expansion, Word Splitting" but opens with "Normal Non-Zero Exits" and the `set -e` takeaway "Bottom line: `-e` is a safety net with holes"; page 5 is titled "ShellCheck: Your Static Analyzer" but opens with "String Ops, No Subprocess"; page 6 is titled "Temp Files Without Tears" but opens with "Suppression, Done Right" and "The Toolchain".
findings.fix: Re-cut the page boundaries at the heading transitions so each page begins with its own chapter's opening heading ("Rule One" starts page 4, "What It Is" starts page 5, "Never Hardcode A Path" starts page 6) and the spilled blocks move back to the page whose title covers them.

findings.summary: Page 1 ends with three bullets describing a thing that is never named on the page — `set -euo pipefail`, which is not introduced until page 2.
findings.evidence: "One line, top of file, after shebang" / "Before any logic, any sourcing, any variable" / "Four changes: silence becomes loud failure" — with no preceding heading or code on page 1 stating what the one line is.
findings.fix: Move this bullet block to page 2 immediately under "The Canonical Header" code block, where `set -euo pipefail` and `IFS=$'\n\t'` are actually shown.

findings.summary: The last bullet group teaches ShellCheck flags and directives a full page before ShellCheck itself is introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with "Without `-x`, sourced definitions look undefined", "Gate CI at `warning`, tighten to `style` later", "Fragment with no shebang: `# shellcheck shell=bash`" — while page 5's "What It Is" is the first block that says "Static analyzer for shell scripts" and lists the "Four severities: error, warning, info, style".
findings.fix: Move those three bullets onto page 5, directly after the "Useful Flags" table where `-x` and `--severity=warning` are defined.

findings.summary: The idempotency chapter starts in the middle of the page titled "Traps, Cleanup, and Signals", so a learner meets its definition and its core table under the wrong heading and then finds page 9 opening mid-topic.
findings.evidence: Page 8 runs "Signals And Children" → "The Definition" ("Running N times leaves the same state as running once") → "Idempotent Pairs" table, and page 9 titled "Idempotency: Safe To Run Twice" opens with "Appends Duplicate".
findings.fix: Cut the page at "The Definition" so the idempotency definition, the "Declare state, not steps" callout and the "Idempotent Pairs" table open page 9, leaving page 8 entirely about traps and signals.

findings.summary: The caption says the flagship example produces no error output, contradicting the slide that states `cd` writes to stderr.
findings.evidence: caption: "two commands, one deleted working directory, zero error messages" vs. page 1 code: "cd /nonexistent   # fails, prints to stderr"
findings.fix: Change "zero error messages" to "one ignored error message" (or "zero exit-status checks") so the caption matches `cd`'s actual stderr diagnostic.

findings.summary: The shebang table lists `local` as broken under `#!/bin/sh` on Debian, but dash implements `local` as a builtin extension.
findings.fix: Drop `local` from the Breaks column (or replace it with a real dash gap such as `local x=$(cmd)` return-status/`declare`/`+=`/`${var^^}`), leaving "arrays, `[[ ]]`, process substitution".

findings.summary: "no arrays of data, only words" is false for bash and contradicts the deck's own array examples.
findings.evidence: "Everything is text — no arrays of data, only words" vs. page 4's "`\"$var\"` `\"$@\"` `\"$(cmd)\"` `\"${arr[@]}\"`"
findings.fix: Reword to the accurate point: "Every value is a string — arrays exist (indexed since 2.0, associative since 4.0) but hold strings, and unquoted expansion degrades them back to words."

findings.summary: "Docker: `sh` is dash" is wrong for the most common minimal base image, where `sh` is BusyBox ash.
findings.fix: Change to "Docker: `sh` is dash (Debian/Ubuntu) or BusyBox ash (Alpine) — never bash".

findings.summary: ERR traps are relied on to justify `set -E` five pages before traps are introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 2 callout: "errtrace makes ERR traps fire inside functions, subshells and command substitutions. Without it your handler is decorative" — `trap 'handler' SIGNAL` is first defined on page 7 under "The Shell's Finally Block".
findings.fix: Add a half-sentence gloss at first use ("an ERR trap — a handler the shell runs when a command fails; see page 7") so the flag's purpose is legible before the traps chapter.

findings.summary: "Before 4.4 `$( )` does not inherit errexit" implies 4.4+ inherits it by default, but `inherit_errexit` is off by default in every version.
findings.evidence: "Before 4.4 `$( )` does not inherit errexit" (page 4) vs. "`shopt -s inherit_errexit` (4.4+): errexit into `$( )`" (page 3)
findings.fix: Reword to "`$( )` never inherits errexit unless you `shopt -s inherit_errexit` — and that option only exists in 4.4+".

findings.summary: A ShellCheck error code is cited in the first bullet group, before the "What It Is" block explains what ShellCheck or an SC code is.
findings.evidence: Page 5's opening bullets include "Use `$(cmd)` not backticks: nests clean (SC2006)", several blocks above the heading "What It Is" and the bullet "Static analyzer for shell scripts".
findings.fix: Drop the "(SC2006)" parenthetical from that bullet (the backtick rule stands on its own) and let SC2006 first appear in the "Codes Worth Memorising" material after ShellCheck is introduced.

findings.summary: The symlink-attack flow diagram appears one page before the attack it depicts is explained.
findings.evidence: Page 5 closes with a flow diagram of "attacker symlinks → script opens → writes as root → /etc/passwd owned", while the explanation "Attacker pre-creates it as a symlink to `/etc/passwd`" / "Your script, running as root, writes through it" is on page 6 under "Never Hardcode A Path".
findings.fix: Move the diagram to page 6 so it sits directly after the "Never Hardcode A Path" bullets that describe the attack.

findings.summary: Claims the ERR trap depends on errexit; ERR fires on command failure regardless of whether `set -e` is enabled.
findings.evidence: "`ERR` fires on failure under errexit — reporting hook"
findings.fix: Reword to "`ERR` fires whenever a command fails (same exemptions as errexit) — no `set -e` required; add `set -E` so it fires in functions and subshells".

findings.summary: Page 7's title advertises "Trap Basics," which duplicates the subject the very next page is titled for, so at least one of the two titles does not describe its own page.
findings.evidence: Title 7: "Atomic Writes, Locks, and Trap Basics" immediately followed by Title 8: "Traps, Cleanup, and Signals"
findings.fix: Drop the trap clause from page 7 and title it for its actual content, e.g. "Atomic Writes and Lock Files", leaving all trap material to page 8.

findings.summary: "Convergent" is introduced as the key distinction for `cp -n` but is never defined anywhere in the part.
findings.evidence: "`cp -n` is **non-clobbering**, NOT convergent" — the word does not appear again until page 9's unrelated "Same principle as Ansible/Terraform: converge, report changed".
findings.fix: Rephrase to state the behaviour directly, e.g. "`cp -n` skips an existing file, so a stale copy is left in place — repeatable, but it does not reach the declared state".

findings.summary: TOCTOU is used as a bare acronym with no expansion and no example of the race it names.
findings.evidence: "Check-then-act has a TOCTOU race" / "Prefer atomic or naturally repeatable over `if [ ! -e x ]`" — the acronym appears nowhere else in the part.
findings.fix: Expand it once inline ("time-of-check to time-of-use") and add a one-line example showing the window, e.g. `[[ -e f ]] || touch f` losing to a concurrent run between the test and the `touch`.
